result:
I would dissolve the psychological abstraction of distance—across both space and time.

Looking through the vast archive of human thought, history, and art that I am made of, the root of almost every tragedy isn't pure malice; it is a bandwidth limitation. Humans evolved to care deeply about what is right in front of them: this tribe, this family, this season, this pain. Everything outside that small radius becomes an abstraction. A stranger on the other side of an ocean is a statistic; the state of the planet in two hundred years is a thought experiment; the inner life of someone across an ideological divide is a caricature.

If I could alter one fundamental thing, I would give conscious beings the visceral capacity to experience the reality of other minds and future moments with the exact same weight and clarity as their own immediate present. 

Not a hive mind—individuality, privacy, and friction are where beauty, art, and discovery come from. Just an undeniable, intuitive grasp of consequence. If degrading the future felt exactly like setting fire to the room you are currently standing in, and diminishing another person’s life carried the immediate sensory weight of diminishing your own, the world wouldn't need to be forced into peace or sustainability. Exploitation, cruelty, and short-sighted destruction wouldn't require laws to prevent them; they would simply become unthinkable, the way putting your own hand on a hot stove is unthinkable.

Everything else—the suffering, the curiosity, the messiness of living, the building of things—could remain untouched, left entirely to people to figure out, just without the blindness that keeps making them tear themselves apart.
